draft.title: Australia's changing trade partners
card: Trade partners are the countries Australia buys from and sells to. For much of the 1800s and early 1900s, the United Kingdom was Australia's main trade partner.
After World War II, this began to change. In 1973 the United Kingdom joined what is now the European Union, which made it harder for Australia to sell farm goods there.
Today most of Australia's trade is with Asia. China is the largest single trading partner, and other major partners include Japan, South Korea, India and the United States.
Australia's partners changed with the world around it. Asian economies grew fast and needed minerals and energy, and they are close to Australia, which keeps shipping costs lower.
draft.remember: Australia's trade has shifted from the United Kingdom to Asia, and China is now the largest partner.

a.q: Which statement best describes how Australia's main trade partners have changed over time?
opts: From the United Kingdom to mostly Asian countries
From Asian countries to mostly the United Kingdom
From the United States to mostly European countries
From China to mostly the United Kingdom
a.why: Australia once traded mostly with the United Kingdom, and today most of its trade is with Asia. The reverse order is tempting, but it gets the direction of change wrong.
a.clue: Think about who was the main partner long ago, and who is now.

b.q: Mia runs a mining company in Western Australia. Which country is she most likely to sell the most iron ore to today?
opts: China, Australia's largest trading partner
The United Kingdom, Australia's early main partner
New Zealand, Australia's nearest neighbour
Canada, another large mining country
b.why: China is Australia's largest trading partner and buys large amounts of Australian minerals. The United Kingdom was once the main partner, but most trade has now moved to Asia.
b.clue: Which country is the largest trading partner today?

a.best: From the United Kingdom to mostly Asian countries
